items.description: The Ledger Book (Lore Item) – Lists a bulk order from an unknown “Mister H. Graves”, including an absurd amount of raw meat and blood packets.  Ambiguous Lore: The Freezer Horror The walk-in freezer is iced shut, but forcing it open (STR DC 14 or tools) reveals a grisly scene:  Several human bodies are stacked like frozen cuts of meat.  Each corpse is missing its head.  Some show bite marks that aren’t human.  A thawed body (with a missing lower half) suddenly twitches, and then crawls forward, screeching. (Roll for initiative!) (What was this place really supplying…?) XP & Survival Value (SV) Action or Loot SV Reward Securing Sweet Cravings Bakery entirely 150 SV Box of Vacuum- Sealed Coffee 20 SV Bag of Sugar (potential crafting material) 10 SV Discovery of The Freezer Horror (Lore) 50 SV Successfully Destroying The Freezer Horror 75 SV Tension Impact  Loud Noises (Breaking cases, gunfire, knocking over racks) → +1d4 Tension  Triggering the Freezer Horror → +1d6 Tension  Explosion from the Oven Gas Leak → +2d6 Tension, alerts zombies within two floors. Enemies & Threats Flesh Rat Swarm A writhing, screeching mass of undead rodents, unnaturally aggressive and partially fused together by necrotic energy.  HP: 20  AC: 12  Bite Swarm: +3 to hit, 2d6 piercing damage  Plague Carrier: Any bite forces a CON Save DC 12 vs. Infection  Disperses if hit by fire or loud noise. The Freezer Horror (Crawling Torso) A half-frozen, headless human corpse that drags itself forward on blackened hands, shrieking without lungs.  HP: 25  AC: 13  Claw Attack: +4 to hit, 1d8 slashing  Death Shriek (Once per fight): Everyone in 20ft makes a WIS Save DC 13 or takes 1d6 psychic damage and suffers disadvantage for one round due to sheer terror.  Can only be permanently killed by fire or decapitation. Survival XP  Clearing the Flesh Rat Nest: +50 SV  Killing the Freezer Horror: +75 SV  Safely looting the bakery: +50 SV  Avoiding combat and stealthily escaping: +100 SV Final Thoughts & Adventure Hooks Sweet Cravings Bakery is a low-threat encounter on  the surface but becomes deadly if players are reckless. The ambiguity of the frozen bodies, the hints at something sinister happening before the outbreak, and the traps and hazards make it a memorable survival horror set-piece. Possible follow-ups: - The name “Mister H. Graves” appears elsewhere in the mall. Who—or what—was he? - The industrial ovens could be repaired and used for food production… or body disposal. - If the Freezer Horror wasn’t the last one… what else is still frozen somewhere in the mall?

actors.name: Alex

source.note: Authored level-one survivor baseline. Role and ability emphasis draw on the module; complete survivor classes are deferred.

actors.biography: Alex was a mall maintenance worker before the outbreak. They know how to force a jammed door and keep moving when a plan falls apart.
actors.personality: Practical and protective. Prefers to hold the front.

actors.name: Sam

source.note: Authored level-one survivor baseline. Role and ability emphasis draw on the module; complete survivor classes are deferred.

actors.biography: Sam worked the early shift at the mall. They listen before opening doors and keep a careful count of everyone in the group.
actors.personality: Watchful and patient. Checks corners before committing.

actors.personality: Steady under pressure. Watches for signs of exhaustion.

actors.name: Robin

actors.personality: Resourceful and cautious. Notices things others leave behind.

effects.text: The directory shows Wanderlust Getaways and Paper Haven to the south. Brewed Awakening and Gourmet Glutton face them across the concourse.
Sunlit beaches stare out from faded posters. Behind the travel desks, two doors lead to the employee office and supply closet.
Notebooks and pens cover the display. Narrow aisles wind between the shelves, with a stockroom at the back.
The espresso machine is silent. Tables crowd the floor, and a stockroom door sits behind the counter.
A sour smell rises from the gourmet shelves. The refrigerated pantry is dark. Something scrapes against a shelf.
A cot and a supply box fit behind the office door. With one way in, this room could shelter the group between supply runs.
A jammed fire shutter seals the east wing. Another route will be needed.
Casey: I can help. Let us get everyone out of here together.
Robin: You are alive. Good. I know where they kept the spare supplies.
Carry newly found supplies to the shelter stockpile. Starting gear and supplies already here do not earn experience. Use Store Finds or deposit individual stacks.
The service manifest records a blocked access passage. The local maintenance response is finite; its cleared state will persist.

objectives.text: Find the temporary shelter in the back office.
Invite Casey to join the expedition.
Invite Robin to join the expedition.
Secure at least 10 SV of scavenged supplies in the shelter stockpile.

expedition.title: A Place to Hold
expedition.briefing: The west entrance offers a foothold. Read the directory, find an office refuge and help the survivors hiding nearby. Check all four shops, clear the threats, then return with at least 10 SV of scavenged supplies. Gather everyone in the back office and use the expedition report board to finish.
expedition.successText: The southwest shops are quiet, four survivors have a place to gather, and the office stockpile can support the next supply run. This is a foothold in the mall. Keep the supplies safe and plan the next expedition.

stages.title: Find Your Bearings
stages.hint: Open the west doors and read the mall directory.

stages.title: A Place to Gather
stages.hint: Inspect Wanderlust's back-office refuge and invite Casey and Robin from the rear rooms.

stages.title: Sweep the Shops
stages.hint: Inspect all four shops and clear the shamblers and runner in the northern shops and Paper Haven.

stages.title: Bring Supplies Home
stages.hint: Secure at least 10 SV of finds at the shelter stockpile. Keep those supplies there for the report.

survivors.values: Values careful scouting, honest warnings and a leader who listens.
Values medical privacy, recovery and mutual care.
Values transparent supplies, shared technical knowledge and practical cooperation.

decisions.title: Sam: The next watch
decisions.text: Sam checks the office door twice. "When we go back out, I need to know we will stop and look before charging in."

choices.text: Promise to hear the scout before committing.
choices.response: Sam nods. "Then I will tell you when something feels wrong."

choices.text: Tell Sam to keep doubts to himself.

decisions.title: Casey: Room to recover
decisions.text: Casey folds a clean cloth. "People need permission to admit they are hurt. We cannot treat every pause as weakness."

choices.text: Make room for honest medical concerns.
choices.response: "Good. I can work with that," Casey says.

choices.text: Insist that everyone must push through.
choices.response: Casey pockets the cloth. "I will still treat them. Even when they are afraid to ask."

decisions.title: Robin: Count what we have
decisions.text: Robin asks for a shared inventory. "No private claims on the supplies we bring home together."

choices.text: Agree to a transparent shared inventory.
choices.response: Robin marks the ledger. "Everyone can see where things went."

choices.text: Reserve the right to conceal supplies.
choices.response: "Then I will count twice," Robin replies.

decisions.title: Contact: The Tinkerer’s Guild
decisions.text: Mara passes on a message from the Guild. They want the maintenance findings shared, rather than hoarded. This contact is an authored refuge scene.

choices.text: Share the findings and credit the recovery crew.
choices.response: Mara sends the notes. The Guild offers friendlier trade terms: five percentage points less markup.

choices.text: Withhold the findings and demand special treatment.
choices.response: Mara relays the demand. The Guild becomes wary of the refuge. Trade terms depend on your resulting standing.

decisions.title: Contact: The Phantom Runners
decisions.text: A runner’s note asks whether the refuge will share accurate hazard reports. Sam and Robin disagree about revealing useful routes.

choices.text: Share warnings without revealing the stockpile.
choices.response: The Runners acknowledge the warning. Sam and Robin agree on a safer reporting rule.

choices.text: Send a misleading report to keep others away.
choices.response: The discrepancy is discovered. Sam distrusts the deception; Robin is uneasy about the fallout.

decisions.title: Contact: The Remnants
decisions.text: A courier from the ex-military Remnants proposes a mutual safety report. Casey insists that civilian medical needs remain confidential.

choices.text: Exchange safety reports while protecting medical privacy.
choices.response: The courier accepts the boundary. Casey and Sam work out a shared reporting routine.

choices.text: Threaten the courier and demand obedience.
choices.response: The courier leaves. Casey and Sam argue about inviting another conflict.

decisions.title: Sam: A private word
decisions.text: Sam offers a more personal conversation after the earlier commitment. "It helps knowing someone will listen."

choices.text: Take time to listen and strengthen the crew.
choices.response: The conversation ends quietly. Sam seems more comfortable working with the others.

choices.text: Explain that you are not ready to discuss it.
choices.response: The boundary is accepted. The earlier conversation still stands.

sites.name: Wanderlust Getaways
sites.bookText:
Wanderlust Getaways 
(Shop #1)
“Brightly colored posters of tropical beaches, snow-
capped mountains, and bustling cityscapes still cling 
to the walls, their edges curled and faded by time. 
The words ‘Your Dream Vacation Awaits!’ feel like a 
cruel joke now, as the only journey left is survival. 
Desks  covered  in  old  brochures  are  overturned, 
spilling pamphlets onto a carpet crusted with dried 
blood. A shattered glass display case in the back 
houses a row of outdated passports, next to a cash 
register that has long since been emptied. The air 
carries the faint scent of mildew and something… 
rotten. A battered suitcase sits upright in the corner, 
its handle extended, as if its owner had been ready to 
leave—but never got the chance.”
General Description
Wanderlust Getaways was once a thriving travel 
agency, filled with eager vacation planners and 
globetrotting dreamers. Now, it’s a grim reminder of a 
world that no longer exists. The room is cluttered with 
travel brochures, old computer terminals with dead 
screens, and an overturned office chair resting beside a 
large, crusted bloodstain.
The store is fairly intact but eerily silent. It has one 
front glass window (partially cracked), a back employee 
office, and a supply closet.

sites.bookText:
Paper Haven (Shop #2)
“Rows of neat, colorful stationery line the shelves—
once a paradise for students and office workers, now 
a forgotten relic of civilization. The scent of old paper 
and dried ink lingers in the still air, mingling with the 
faint  mustiness  of  neglect.  Handwritten  notes  and 
planners  are  scattered  across  the  counters, 
abandoned mid-thought, as if their owners vanished 
in an instant. A toppled display rack spills notebooks 
across the floor, their pages torn and stained with 
something dark. A soft scratching sound echoes from 
the backroom, like something rifling through forgotten 
supplies…”
General Description
Once a quaint stationery shop catering to students and 
professionals, Paper Haven now serves as an eerie 
reminder of abandoned plans and unfinished business. 
Its shelves remain surprisingly well-stocked with office 
supplies, journals, art materials, and an assortment of 
crafting tools. A locked supply closet in the back holds 
more valuable goods, but something—or someone—
has already made a mess of the storage area.

sites.name: Brewed Awakening
sites.bookText:
Brewed Awakening (Shop 
#3)
Read-Aloud:
“The stale scent of coffee lingers in the air, mixing with 
the faint stench of decay. Rows of overturned chairs 
and scattered ceramic mugs create an abandoned 
battlefield of shattered porcelain and dried-up espresso 
spills. A lone menu board flickers above the counter, its 
neon glow barely holding on, advertising drinks no one 
will ever order again. The espresso machine hisses 
occasionally, though no one touches it. A trail of 
smeared footprints leads to the back storage room, 
disappearing into the dark. Something—someone—was 
here recently… or still is.”
General Description
Brewed Awakening was once the trendiest café in the 
mall, a hotspot for caffeine addicts, overworked 
students, and pretentious coffee snobs. Now, it’s a 
haunting relic of normal life. The coffee bar is still 
partially stocked, but the pastries in the display case are 
now petrified lumps. A few toppled tables and 
cushioned chairs provide potential cover or barricades. 
The back storage room is eerily dark, its door slightly 
ajar.

Layout: Open seating area with scattered 
tables and chairs, long barista counter, menu 
boards still faintly glowing. Back room with 
storage shelves and an employee break area. 
A side door leads to the service corridor.

Threats: Unseen dangers lurk in the dark. 
Something is inside the back storage room.

Hazards: Spilled coffee bags create slippery 
surfaces (Dexterity DC 12 to avoid falling). 
Hidden glass shards underfoot (Constitution 
DC 12 or take 1d4 bleeding damage).
Encounter Elements & 
Random Events (roll 1d6 on 
entry)
d6 Roll Event
1
Espresso Machine Hiss: The 
machine inexplicably sputters and 
releases a loud burst of steam. 
(+1d4 Tension, 25% chance to 
attract 1d4 Shamblers)
2
Knock from Storage Room: A 
muffled sound echoes from behind 
the door, as if someone—or 
something—is trapped inside.
3
Ceiling Drip: A slow, rhythmic 
dripping from the ceiling—except 
it’s not water. (DM’s choice: blood, 
oil, or something alien.)
4
Survivor Graffiti: A message 
scrawled in coffee on the wall 
reads: “DON’T DRINK IT.” But 
why?
5
Phantom Aroma: The air suddenly 
smells like freshly brewed coffee. 
There is no coffee brewing.
6
Spilled Sugar Swarm: A pile of 
sugar has been knocked over, 
but the writhing movement 
inside reveals it is infested with 
roaches. (Will players dare to 
scavenge food here?)
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Sealed Bag of Coffee Beans – 
Non-perishable, boosts morale, 
 200 

Zombie Mall
 
Lower Level
trade value (15 SV).
2
Crowbar (Improvised Weapon) – 
1d8 bludgeoning, advantage on 
opening locked doors (30 SV).
3
Cold Brew Growler (Full) – 
Restores stamina, can be traded for 
20 SV. Has 5 servings.
4
Barista Apron (Light Armor, AC 
11) – Surprisingly durable, 
advantage on disguise rolls when 
dealing with certain survivor factions 
(15 SV).
5
Security Camera Console – If 
powered, can be used to check mall 
hallways (potential lore clue).
6
Loyalty Card (With 9/10 Stamps) 
– If humor is needed, the 10th 
stamp entitles a player to a “free 
latte” (if they ever find an 
untainted one).
Back Storage Room (Optional 
Encounter)
The storage room door is slightly ajar, revealing 
darkness and the faint sound of shuffling. Inside, 
players will find:

Tied-Up Survivor (50% Chance) – An 
exhausted man named Eddie, bound and 
gagged, eyes wide with terror. He will 
frantically shake his head if players try to 
free him. If they do, roll 1d4:
o
1-2: He was restrained for a reason—
he turns into a zombie within minutes!
o
3-4: He is actually a paranoid survivor 
who will flee at the first opportunity 
unless convinced to stay.

Infected Barista Zombie (Guaranteed) – A 
former employee is lurking inside, partially 
fused with mold-covered burlap coffee 
sacks. She lunges if disturbed.

Locked Employee Locker – Requires 
lockpicking (Dexterity DC 15) or brute force 
(Strength DC 14). Inside:
o
A note: “BioDyne shipment delayed. 
DO NOT serve the samples.”
o
Mysterious “Special Reserve” 
Coffee Canister (TBD effect—could 
be an experimental stimulant or 
something worse).
o
A stun baton (1d6 electric damage, 
3 charges left).
Ambiguous Lore
The shop contains subtle hints about the origins of the 
outbreak, but they contradict each other:
d4 
Roll
Ambiguous Clue
1
A receipt labeled “BioDyne Corp 
Special Blend – Experimental Lot 
#X9-13”, suggesting a connection to 
corporate bio-research.
2
A handwritten journal entry in the 
employee breakroom: “The old man 
kept saying ‘the cup of wrath has 
been poured out.’ He wouldn’t stop 
screaming about seals breaking. We 
had to throw him out.”
3
A faded newspaper clipping about 
a local cult’s coffee shop boycott, 
citing “demonic influences in 
caffeine culture.”
4
A radio broadcast recording 
looping in the storage room: 
“Avoid contamination vectors. Do 
NOT consume tainted fluids. The 
pathogen thrives in liquid 
mediums.”


Making noise (knocking over furniture, 
activating machines) increases Tension by 
+1d6.

If the back storage room door is opened 
without caution, increase Tension by +2d6.

If the survivor (if present) panics and runs 
into the mall screaming, increase Tension by 
+3d6.

restrains target if failed STR save)
Mold-Spore Zombie (Optional)

AC: 13

HP: 22

Special Ability: “Coughs up spores” – Players 
in melee range must roll CON DC 14 or gain 
1d4 Infection Points.

sites.name: Gourmet Glutton
sites.bookText:
Gourmet Glutton (Shop #4)
“The air in this high-end specialty food store is thick 
with  the  mingling  scents  of  expired  truffle  oil  and 
rotting  cheese.  Gilded  shelves,  once  stocked  with 
delicacies for the wealthy, now hold shattered glass 
jars and tumbled-over wicker baskets. A half-eaten 
wheel of Brie sits on the counter, its moldy remains 
swarming with flies. A grand, broken display case 
labeled ‘Luxury Imported Goods’ still contains a few 
sealed  tins  of  caviar—if  you  dare  to  trust  them. 
Somewhere  in  the  back,  something  drips  steadily, 
echoing through the eerie silence. You’re not alone.”
Description

Layout: A boutique-style gourmet shop with 
marble counters, wooden display shelves, and 
a dimly lit refrigerated section in the back.

Threats:
o
1d6 Rot-Gut Shamblers (slow, 
bloated corpses with acidic bile, see 
below).
o
Hidden Feasters – Some “dead” 
bodies slumped in the aisle may 
actually be lying in wait.

Hazards:
o
Slick Floors – Spilled olive oil and 
broken wine bottles create slippery 
patches (DEX DC 14 to avoid falling, 
failure = prone).
o
Rotten Air – The mix of expired dairy 
and spoiled meats makes breathing 
unpleasant (CON save DC 12 or suffer 
disadvantage on perception checks for 
10 minutes).
Encounter Elements
Environmental Hazards & Traps (roll 1d4 on entry)
d4 Roll Hazard
1
Tainted Air – Spoiled food gases 
cause mild nausea (CON save DC 
13 or disadvantage on attacks for 
1d6 minutes).
 202

Lower Level
2

collapses if disturbed (DEX DC 14 
or take 2d6 bludgeoning and +1d6 
Tension).
3

used here, there’s a 50% chance of 
a small explosion (3d6 fire damage, 
+2d6 Tension).
4

rats bursts from the back room 
(treat as 1d4 Swarm of Rats).

d6

traps.

– Roll CON DC 14 if consumed

before convulsing.





o

The Taster (Cursed Corpse)




1.

nibbles something before engaging.
2.
Unholy Appetite: Immune to poison 
and can regain HP if it consumes a 
living creature’s flesh (1d8 heal per 
bite).





Goods: Variable SV (~50-100 total)

SV
Final Notes
Gourmet Glutton is a tense, resource-rich area but 
comes with high risk. Between gas leaks, exploding 
zombies, hidden threats, and possibly cursed lore, 
it’s not just about scavenging—it’s about survival.
Can be turned into a supply depot if secured properly, 
though the smell may attract more undead over time…

sites.name: Daily Grind
sites.bookText:
Daily Grind (Coffee Shop 
#5)
The air is thick with the bitter scent of old espresso 
grounds and burnt milk. Rows of untouched paper 
cups still sit stacked behind the counter, waiting for a 
morning  rush  that  will  never  come.  A  half-eaten 
muffin, dried and fossilized, remains on a lonely table 
as if someone just stepped away—but never came 
back.  The  espresso  machine  hums  faintly, 
inexplicably  powered,  its  blinking  lights  an  eerie 
contrast to the silence. A sticky note on the register 
reads: “Be right back. Lock up if you leave.” You hear 
a faint drip—water, or something else—coming from 
the employee-only storage room…
General Description
Daily Grind was once a popular franchise coffee shop, 
its warm wooden décor and inviting smells luring in tired 
shoppers. Now, its charm has faded into decay. The 
front counter remains mostly intact, its espresso 
machine somehow still operational. Behind the counter, 
scattered bags of coffee beans, sugar packets, and 
syrups offer potential supplies. The tables and chairs 
have been overturned, some barricading a back storage 
door that something has clearly tried to break through.
The sound of dripping liquid comes from the back, 
where a shattered cold brew dispenser is still slowly 
leaking onto the floor. The air is unsettlingly warm, and 
the smell of stale pastries barely covers something 
rotting.
Encounter Elements

storage room door is blocked with

inside is scratching at it. (If

emerge.)

old milk fell and curdled—badly. If 
disturbed, it releases a nauseating 
stench (Constitution DC 12 or

minutes).
3

rigging a coffee machine to a gas 
line for a makeshift flamethrower. 
The line is leaking. A single spark 
will cause an explosion (3d6 fire 
damage, 15ft radius).
4

machine lets out a loud, 
mechanical hissing. Roll a 
Perception (DC 14) check. If

someone (or something) is 
making the sound. (Paranoia 
Effect: +1d4 Tension.)

Survival XP Summary

Securing Daily Grind: 250 SV

Clearing Threats: 100 SV

Using Espresso Machine for Morale Boost: 
+10 SV per use (but increases Tension)

Finding Lore Clues: 50-75 SV
Final Notes
Daily Grind is a high-risk, high-reward location. 
Players can secure morale boosts and supplies, but 
careless actions can quickly escalate Tension, leading 
to a horde event. The espresso machine is a fun but 
dangerous temptation—boosting morale but making 
way too much noise. If the storage barricade is 
broken, it could trigger a mini-dungeon within the 
store as zombies spill into the space.
This location also serves as a nexus for multiple story 
clues—was the outbreak biological, supernatural, or 
something else entirely? Players may never know for 
sure, but this shop holds some very suggestive 
breadcrumbs.

sites.name: Clear Vision
sites.bookText:
Clear Vision (Shop #6)
“A sickly green light flickers through the cracked glass 
storefront,  casting  warped  shadows  over  rows  of 
display cases filled with untouched eyeglasses. Some 
frames remain neatly arranged on velvet-lined trays, 
while  others  lay  scattered,  crushed  underfoot.  A 
shattered  mirror  stretches  along  the  back  wall,  its 
fragmented  reflection  multiplying  the  store’s  eerie 
stillness.  A  faint  chemical  smell  lingers  in  the  air, 
blending with the staleness of long-abandoned retail. 
The  silence  is  nearly  absolute—except  for  the 
occasional tap tap tap of something moving behind 
the counter.”
General Description
Once a stylish optical shop offering designer frames 
and high-end prescription lenses, Clear Vision now 
stands eerily intact, its wares largely untouched. Its 
position near the main concourse made it one of the 
first places looters passed by, but few seemed 
interested in stealing eyewear. The interior is dimly lit, 
with display counters still locked and a storage area 
hidden in the back.

If the storage room is searched, roll 1d6. On a 5 or 6,

Survival Strategy & Unique 
Uses

Barricade Potential – The shop’s metal 
security gate can be manually lowered and 
locked (DC 16 Strength to break through).

Vision Aids – Players with poor eyesight can 
find glasses to counteract blurry vision 
penalties.

Darkness Strategy – If players lure zombies 
into the dark storage room, they suffer 
disadvantage on attack rolls, while The 
Optometrist does not.

Deception Potential – The binoculars can be 
used to scout, or players can place 
mannequins at the storefront to confuse 
zombies.
Final Thoughts
Clear Vision is a small but eerie encounter that adds 
psychological horror, a unique undead enemy, and 
potential lore clues to the mall’s mysterious 
apocalypse. Whether the players fight The Optometrist 
or simply loot what they can and flee, the experience 
will linger long after they leave.

actions.text: A burnt religious pamphlet referencing the “Plague of Blinded  Sinners”, warning that “only those with clear vision shall be spared the dark awakening.” Special Encounter: “The Optometrist” (Unique Undead) If the storage room is searched, roll 1d6. On a 5 or 6, the Optometrist emerges.  Once the store’s owner, he now lurks in the darkness, hunched and twitching.  His eyes have been surgically removed, but he still sees perfectly.  He whispers cryptic phrases about “perfect vision” before attacking.  His bite carries a unique infection, causing hallucinations instead of disease.  If defeated, players find a BioDyne contact lens case in his pocket, labeled “Experimental Retinal Enhancement – Do Not Use.” The Optometrist (Unique Undead) AC: 14 HP: 22 Speed: 30 ft (ignores darkness penalties) Attacks: o Scalpel Slash: +4 to hit, 1d6+2 slashing damage o Madness Bite: +3 to hit, 1d4 piercing + Hallucination Effect Special Ability: “I See You” 3. The first survivor he stares at must roll a DC 14 Wisdom Save or suffer temporary hallucinations, imposing Disadvantage on all Perception checks for 1 hour. 4. If bitten twice, hallucinations become permanent until treated with medical aid or extreme rest. Weakness: Bright light (stunned for 1 round when hit by direct light sources). Hidden Crawler – Lying under the counter, grabbing ankles (DC 13 Dex to avoid).
Swarm of Eyeball Spiders – Tiny, reanimated eyes with legs  d6 Roll Zombie/Threat Type (1d4 damage on contact, easily crushed).
The Optometrist – If not already encountered, he awakens in the back room.

Mannequin Mimic – A shop mannequin lurches forward, attacking as a 1HD zombie but resistant to non-bladed damage. Survival Strategy & Unique Uses  Barricade Potential – The shop’s metal security gate can be manually lowered and locked (DC 16 Strength to break through).  Vision Aids – Players with poor eyesight can find glasses to counteract blurry vision penalties.  Darkness Strategy – If players lure zombies into the dark storage room, they suffer disadvantage on attack rolls, while The Optometrist does not.  Deception Potential – The binoculars can be used to scout, or players can place mannequins at the storefront to confuse zombies. Final Thoughts Clear Vision is a small but eerie encounter that adds psychological horror, a unique undead enemy, and potential lore clues to the mall’s mysterious apocalypse. Whether the players fight The Optometrist or simply loot what they can and flee, the experience will linger long after they leave.

sites.name: MegaMart
sites.bookText:
MegaMart (Shop #7) – The 
Hollowed-Out 
Supermarket
“Rows of empty shelves stretch before you, stripped 
bare  of  their  former  bounty.  Shopping  carts  lie 
abandoned,  some  overturned,  their  wheels  still 
creaking eerily. Fluorescent lights flicker overhead, 
buzzing like distant flies over carrion. The smell of 
rotting produce lingers in the air, mingling with the 
metallic tang of dried blood smeared across the floor. 
Somewhere  deeper  inside,  a  faint  scraping  sound 
echoes  through  the  aisles.  Either  something—or 
someone—is still here.”
General Description
MegaMart, once a bustling supermarket, is now a 
hollowed-out husk of its former self. Looters and 
desperate survivors have long since picked over its 
shelves, leaving behind only scraps. However, this 
cavernous space still holds secrets—hidden 
storerooms, overlooked caches, and an ominous 
presence lurking in the unlit depths of the refrigerated 
section.

Layout: A wide-open space with towering, 
near-empty shelves, scattered debris, and 
narrow aisles. The loading dock in the back 
leads outside, while a manager’s office 
overlooks the store from a second floor.

Threats: Undead lurk in the dark corners—
some trapped behind barricades, others 
disguised as corpses amid fallen shoppers.

Hazards: Slippery floors, unstable shelving, 
and biohazards (rotting food, contaminated 
water).
Environmental Hazards & 
Traps (roll 1d6 on entry)
d6 Roll Hazard
1
Collapsing Shelf: A towering 
display of canned goods topples, 
causing 1d8 bludgeoning damage 
and a DC 14 Dexterity save to 
avoid being pinned. The crash 
increases Tension by +2d6.
2

the wrong freezer releases a cloud

sites.name: Sharp Sight
sites.bookText:
Sharp Sight (Shop #8)
“A shattered glass display crunches underfoot as you 
step  into  what  was  once  a  high-end  eyewear 
boutique. The walls are lined with broken shelves, 
expensive frames still neatly arranged beneath layers 
of dust. A cracked mirror near the register distorts 
your reflection, twisting your features into something 
grotesque.  Scattered  lenses  reflect  the  dim  light, 
making the floor look like a starry sky of jagged glass. 
The faint sound of skittering movement echoes from 
the back room—something is still here, hiding in the 
gloom.”
General Description
Sharp Sight was once a sleek boutique specializing in 
luxury eyewear—designer sunglasses, high-end 
prescription glasses, and cutting-edge lens technology. 
Now, it’s a wasteland of shattered display cases, 
overturned shelving, and half-looted inventory.

Layout:
o
The front showroom is mostly 
destroyed—glass shards everywhere, 
expensive but now mostly useless 
frames on display.
o
A register counter with a small, 
overturned safe sits near the entrance.
o
A back storage room remains closed
—something has barricaded the door 
from the inside.
o
A fitting mirror, cracked and fogged 
over, takes up a large section of the 
wall. Looking into it for too long makes 
you uneasy.
o
A ceiling air vent has been recently 
disturbed, the grate barely hanging on.

Threats:
o
Hidden Lurker (1) – A Crawler 
Zombie (half-bodied, dragging itself) 
waits under the main counter.
o
Ceiling Creeper (1) – A zombie (or 
something worse) inside the vent may 
drop down if disturbed.
o
Back Room Mystery – Something 
alive is in the storage room, but it 
hasn’t made itself known… yet.

Hazards:
o
Glass Shard Field – Moving too 
quickly through the shop risks injury 
(1d4 damage per 10ft, negated with 
shoes or careful movement).
o
Cracked Mirror Effect – Staring into 
the mirror for more than a few seconds 
causes an unsettling illusion. (Roll 
1d6: 1-3 nothing, 4-5 strange reflection 
behavior, 6 induces paranoia).
o
Collapsing Shelves – A poorly 
balanced display can tip over if 
bumped, causing 1d6 bludgeoning 
damage and loud noise (+2d4 
Tension).

vision (low-light bonus), worth 75 
SV.

SV).

whisper from the cracked mirror. It 
sounds like their own voice.
2
Survivor’s Corpse in Vent – A 
rotting body tumbles out, tangled in 
electrical wires. What were they 
hiding?
3
Loud Security Alarm – If 
disturbed, the counter’s old alarm 
system screeches, drawing 
zombies nearby.
4
Shadow in Reflection – Looking 
into the mirror, players see an extra 
figure that isn’t there in real life.
5
The Glass Shatters… Slowly – A 
mirror in the back cracks, forming 
unreadable symbols.
6
Nothing Happens… but 
something feels wrong.
Escape Routes & Tactical 
Considerations

Back Room Door (Locked, DC 14) – Leads to 
maintenance tunnels.

Ceiling Vent (Crawlspace Option) – Can be 
entered if players clear the Creeper Zombie.

Front Door – Can be barricaded to secure the 
location or smashed for a quick exit 
(increases Tension).
Final Notes
Sharp Sight is a tense, eerie location designed for 
psychological horror and subtle clues rather than 
outright combat. While zombies lurk, the real terror lies 
in the unsettling mirror-based anomalies, cryptic 
notes, and the suspicion that something else was at 
play here beyond a simple infection.

Is the cracked mirror just a mirror?

Why did BioDyne experiment with vision 
enhancement lenses?

What was the last survivor trying to see—or 
trying to avoid looking at?
Players might leave with valuable loot, useful clues, 
or more questions than answers. Either way… they 
won’t look at their reflections the same way again.

actions.name: Nothing Happens… but something feels wrong. Escape Routes & Tacti
actions.text: Nothing Happens… but something feels wrong. Escape Routes & Tactical Considerations  Back Room Door (Locked, DC 14) – Leads to maintenance tunnels.  Ceiling Vent (Crawlspace Option) – Can be entered if players clear the Creeper Zombie.  Front Door – Can be barricaded to secure the location or smashed for a quick exit (increases Tension). Final Notes Sharp Sight is a tense, eerie location designed for psychological horror and subtle clues rather than outright combat. While zombies lurk, the real terror lies in the unsettling mirror-based anomalies, cryptic notes, and the suspicion that something else was at play here beyond a simple infection.  Is the cracked mirror just a mirror?  Why did BioDyne experiment with vision enhancement lenses?  What was the last survivor trying to see—or trying to avoid looking at? Players might leave with valuable loot, useful clues, or more questions than answers. Either way… they won’t look at their reflections the same way again.

sites.name: Sweet Cravings Bakery
sites.bookText:
Sweet Cravings Bakery 
(Shop #9)
The air is thick with the sickly-sweet scent of rot and 
sugar. Rows of glass display cases, once filled with 
delicate pastries, are now smeared with old mold and 
crumbling confections. A flickering neon sign hums 
above the counter, casting a sickly pink glow over rat-
gnawed cupcake boxes. Flies buzz lazily over a once-
grand wedding cake, now home to writhing maggots. 
The tiled floor is sticky—though whether from frosting, 
spilled soda, or something far worse is unclear. In the 
dim kitchen beyond, the rhythmic skittering of unseen 
vermin echoes from the darkness…”
General Description
Once a bustling bakery known for its elaborate cakes 
and warm atmosphere, Sweet Cravings Bakery is now 
a festering ruin of abandoned decadence. Its pink-and-
white striped decor is now stained and peeling, while 
rats and cockroaches have made a feast of whatever 
remains. The storefront is mostly intact, but the 
kitchen in the back holds dangers beyond just spoiled 
food.

Layout: The front counter holds shattered 
 215 

Lower Level
 
Zombie Mall
display cases, a register with a long-silent 
receipt printer, and a self-serve coffee station. 
The kitchen in the back contains large 
industrial ovens, storage racks filled with moldy 
ingredients, and a massive walk-in freezer with 
something ominous frozen inside.

Threats: (Roll 1d4 upon entry)
1.
Nothing—Just Rats. (For now…)

(Hungry, covered in flour, mindlessly

hunger)

Ambiguous Lore: The Freezer 
Horror
The walk-in freezer is iced shut, but forcing it open 
(STR DC 14 or tools) reveals a grisly scene:

Several human bodies are stacked like 
frozen cuts of meat.

Each corpse is missing its head.

Some show bite marks that aren’t human.

A thawed body (with a missing lower half) 
suddenly twitches, and then crawls forward, 
screeching. (Roll for initiative!)
(What was this place really supplying…?)

Tension

Tension, alerts zombies within two floors.
Enemies & Threats
Flesh Rat Swarm
A writhing, screeching mass of undead rodents, 
unnaturally aggressive and partially fused together by 
necrotic energy.

HP: 20

AC: 12

Bite Swarm: +3 to hit, 2d6 piercing damage

Plague Carrier: Any bite forces a CON Save 
DC 12 vs. Infection

Disperses if hit by fire or loud noise.
The Freezer Horror (Crawling Torso)
A half-frozen, headless human corpse that drags 
itself forward on blackened hands, shrieking 
without lungs.

HP: 25

AC: 13

Claw Attack: +4 to hit, 1d8 slashing

Death Shriek (Once per fight): Everyone in 
20ft makes a WIS Save DC 13 or takes 1d6 
psychic damage and suffers disadvantage 
for one round due to sheer terror.

Can only be permanently killed by fire or 
decapitation.
Survival XP

Clearing the Flesh Rat Nest: +50 SV

Killing the Freezer Horror: +75 SV

Safely looting the bakery: +50 SV

Avoiding combat and stealthily escaping: 
+100 SV
Final Thoughts & 
Adventure Hooks
Sweet Cravings Bakery is a low-threat encounter on 
 217

Zombie Mall
the surface but becomes deadly if players are 
reckless. The ambiguity of the frozen bodies, the 
hints at something sinister happening before the 
outbreak, and the traps and hazards make it a 
memorable survival horror set-piece.
Possible follow-ups: - The name “Mister H. Graves” 
appears elsewhere in the mall. Who—or what—was 
he?
- The industrial ovens could be repaired and used for 
food production… or body disposal.
- If the Freezer Horror wasn’t the last one… what 
else is still frozen somewhere in the mall?

sites.bookText:
Urban Nest (Store #10)
“The air inside Urban Nest is thick with the cloying 
scent  of  forgotten  potpourri.  Rows  of  decorative 
pillows,  long  coated  in  dust,  line  the  shelves  like 
faded  trophies  of  a  lost  world.  Ceramic  vases, 
artificial plants, and candle displays sit undisturbed, 
their price tags still attached as if waiting for shoppers 
that will never return. A rack of wind chimes tinkles 
softly in an unfelt breeze, the sound eerily melodic in 
the silence. Something shifts in the dimly lit back aisle
—perhaps  just  settling  debris…  or  something 
watching from the shadows.”
Description

Layout: Urban Nest is a medium-sized home 
décor store packed with fragile furniture, 
decorative trinkets, and cluttered aisles. 
The back stockroom is locked, while the 
register counter has a display of expensive 
scented candles, their wicks long melted into 
wax puddles.

Threats:
o
1d4 Shamblers wandering aimlessly, 
tangled in curtains or lodged between 
shelving units.
o
1 Porcelain Brute (a zombie encased 
in ceramic armor, slow but tough) 
slumped in a recliner.

Hazards:
o
Toppling Shelves: Any loud 
movement (failed DEX check DC 12) 
causes precarious shelves to fall over, 
adding 1d4 to Mall Tension and 
potentially pinning a survivor (STR 
DC 14 to escape).
o
Scent Trap: If disturbed, a large bag 
of potpourri explodes into a thick, 
choking cloud, imposing 
disadvantage on Perception checks for 
1d4 rounds.
o
Wax Spill: The candle aisle is slick 
with hardened wax—failing a DC 13 
Dexterity save results in slipping 
(prone for 1 turn).

The Candle Hermit (Optional

scented candles cause zombies to ignore 
the area for 1d6 days (unless another event 
draws them in).

they act as an early warning system, 
granting a +2 bonus to Perception checks for 
spotting approaching threats.

If fire is used irresponsibly, the store can 
burn down, permanently destroying all loot 
but causing a massive +5d6 Tension spike.

sites.bookText:
Bloom & Grow (Shop #11)
“A wall of green spills out from the shattered glass 
entrance of this overgrown garden center. Thick vines 
coil around empty metal shelves, reaching towards 
the flickering overhead lights. Bags of long-spoiled 
soil spill across the cracked tile floor, their contents 
mingling  with  scattered  gardening  tools  and  fallen 
pots. The air is damp with the scent of mildew and 
something  sweetly  rotten.  Occasionally,  a  leaf 
twitches—not from wind, but as if something unseen 
lurks beneath the tangled vegetation…”

Zombie Mall
 
Lower Level
General Description
Once a thriving garden center, Bloom & Grow is now 
an eerie jungle in miniature, with creeping vines, 
overturned planters, and patches of unchecked fungal 
growth reclaiming the space.
Layout:

A central greenhouse with glass walls, many 
of which are now shattered.

Rows of abandoned gardening supplies, 
from shovels and pruners to bags of mulch.

A storage room in the back, its heavy door 
slightly ajar.

A collapsed shelving unit blocks part of the 
shop, requiring Strength (DC 14) or Dexterity 
(DC 15) to navigate safely.

Rainwater puddles from a broken skylight 
feed a fungal infestation in the far corner.
Threats:

Vine Zombies (1d4+1) – Half-absorbed 
corpses entangled in creeping ivy. Slow but 
resilient.

Spore Clouds – Disturbed fungal growths 
release a spore burst (Constitution Save DC 
12 or suffer 1d4 Poison damage and 
disadvantage on Perception for 1 hour).

Something Unseen Moves in the 
Greenhouse… (See special encounter below.)

Traps (Roll 1d4 when 
players enter the store.)

for 1 minute).

unless cleared with a blade.
4

mummified corpse wrapped in 
vines isn’t quite dead. 
(Ambushes first player who 
steps near it; Dex DC 14 to avoid 
grapple.)

rusted key. (See “Ambiguous

d4 Roll Clue Found

clipboard with notes about

and “rapid regenerative properties 
beyond known botany.”
2

detailing “The Green Awakening” 
and “gifts bestowed upon those 
who offer their flesh to the Blooming 
One.”
3

Mentions a “Category-3 Biohazard 
Containment Failure” and a 
directive to “burn all organic matter 
within perimeter.”
4
Survivor’s Journal – Entries

inside the vines, whispering my 
name. I should not have listened. 
I should not have eaten the fruit.”
Special Encounter – The 
Blooming One (Optional 
Mini-Boss)

HP: 35

AC: 14 (natural bark armor)

Attack: Vine Whip (1d8, 10ft reach, +Grapple)

Special: Regeneration (Heals 5 HP per round 
unless exposed to fire.)

Weakness: Fire deals double damage.
Deep within the greenhouse, a grotesque humanoid 
shape stands partially fused to the vines, its skin 
replaced by twisting roots. It moves slowly, deliberately, 
whispering in a language no one should understand. If 
left undisturbed, it offers a pact—consume its 
forbidden fruit for temporary enhancements… at a 
cost. (Will you accept its gift?)

takes on a bark-like texture (-1 
Charisma).
4
Seeded Flesh – Player is 
infected. In 1d6 days, they must 
pass a Constitution Save (DC 15) 
or begin sprouting vines.

sites.name: Soundwave Records
sites.bookText:
Soundwave Records (Shop 
#12)
“The air inside Soundwave Records is thick with dust, 
the scent of old vinyl mixing with a faint metallic tang. 
Rows of cracked plastic record sleeves sit in warped 
bins, their faded covers depicting forgotten rock stars 
and jazz legends. A display stand showcasing ‘The 
Greatest Hits of 2012’ lies toppled near the entrance, 
its contents scattered like a fallen shrine to a lost era. 
Against the back wall, a broken neon sign flickers 
weakly,  buzzing  like  an  insect  trapped  in  a  light 
fixture.  Something  about  this  place  hums  with 
unnatural energy—perhaps it’s just the speakers left 
connected  to  battery-powered  radios,  whispering 
static  and  half-buried  voices  from  an  empty 
frequency. Or maybe it’s something else entirely…”
General Description
Soundwave Records was once a vibrant hub for music 
lovers, selling vinyl records, vintage turntables, and 
high-end audio equipment. Now, it’s a ghost of itself, 
the shelves looted of most popular albums while 
forgotten genres gather dust. The back storage room 
remains locked, and an old battery-powered radio in the 
corner continues to play a garbled broadcast that loops 
endlessly, though no one is around to tune it.
Layout

Main Floor: Rows of record bins, listening 
booths, display shelves filled with audio 
equipment.

Back Room: Locked storage area with spare 
audio gear and possibly something lurking.

Ceiling Speakers: Some still work, potentially 
useful or hazardous.

sites.name: Second Time Around
sites.bookText:
Second Time Around 
(Shop #13)
“Dusty racks of secondhand clothes line the walls, 
their faded colors and outdated styles frozen in time. 
Mismatched furniture—floral couches, battered end 
tables, and wobbly wooden chairs—create a maze of 
forgotten  relics.  The  air  is  thick  with  the  scent  of 
mothballs, old perfume, and something sour you can’t 
quite place. A fitting room curtain flutters despite the 
lack of wind. Somewhere in the dim aisles, a faint 
creak  echoes—was  that  just  the  old  floorboards 
settling… or something else moving?”
General Description
Second Time Around is a sprawling thrift store, filled 
with discarded fashion, old furniture, and forgotten 
oddities. The cluttered layout makes visibility poor, 
forcing survivors to weave through narrow aisles and 
maneuver past towering piles of stacked junk.
Some fitting rooms are closed, their interiors 
unknown. A checkout counter near the front holds a 
register, while an employee breakroom in the back 
may offer more than just a place to rest… if you can get 
inside.
Encounter Elements
Environmental Hazards & Traps (roll 1d4 on entry)
d4 Roll Hazard
1
Collapsing Clothing Rack – A 
precariously balanced rack topples 
when nudged. Causes 1d6 damage 
and forces a DEX save (DC 13) or 
make loud noise (+1d4 Tension).
2

Looks like a person at first glance. 
On a failed WIS save (DC 12), a 
survivor panics, making immediate 
noise (+2 Tension).
3
Creaking Floorboards – Every 
step past the furniture section risks 
a DEX check (DC 14) or makes 
loud creaks (+1d6 Tension).
4

into an old donation bin releases 
a cloud of spores (CON save DC 
13 or suffer 1 level of 
exhaustion).

– Rusty but functional (1d8 slashing,

Restores 1d6 HP, worth 15 SV.

suggest its connection to the greater mall mystery.

sites.name: Pedal Power
sites.bookText:
Pedal Power (Shop #14)
“The scent of rubber and rust lingers in the air as you 
step inside the bicycle shop. Rows of mountain bikes 
and road racers hang suspended from the ceiling, 
their frames swaying slightly as if disturbed by an 
unseen  force.  Broken  glass  from  the  shattered 
storefront  crunches  underfoot.  A  long,  overturned 
repair  counter  creates  a  crude  barricade  near  the 
back, behind which several bike tires and repair tools 
are scattered. A half-eaten energy bar rests on the 
counter—disturbingly fresh. The back storage room is 
slightly ajar, a dim flickering light within hinting at 
movement.”
Description

Layout:
o
A compact retail space cluttered with 
hanging bikes, parts bins, and deflated 
tires.
o
A repair counter in the center, 
partially barricaded with scrap metal 
and old tires.
o
The storage room in the back 
contains tools, fuel canisters, and 
possibly survivors (or worse).
o
The front windows are shattered, 
leaving it exposed to the concourse.

Threats: (Roll 1d6 when entering to 
determine threats)
d6 Roll Threat Type
1-2
Shamblers (2d4) – Trapped inside 
when the outbreak started.
3-4
Crawler Zombies (1d4) – Hidden 
under shelves, latching onto ankles.
5
“Cycling Dead” (1 Brute Zombie 
on a bike) – A massive zombified 
cyclist tangled in the spokes of a 
high-end road bike.
6
The Speed Freak (Human Raider, 
See Below) – A deranged 
survivor hoarding bike parts, 
twitchy and unpredictable.

Hazards:
d4 Roll Hazard
1
Hanging Bike Trap: A loose bike 
falls from the ceiling if disturbed 
(1d8 damage, Dex DC 14 to avoid).
 228 

Zombie Mall
 
Lower Level
2
Oil Spill: Greasy floor near the 
repair station (Dex DC 12 or fall 
prone).
3
Storage Room Alarm: A motion-
sensitive alarm beeps loudly if the 
storage door is opened incorrectly 
(+2d6 Tension).
4
Loose Brake Cables: Sharp 
cables dangling from a 
workbench can cause 1d6 
slashing damage if mishandled.
Interactables & Loot
(Players can search for supplies, but each attempt risks 
attracting attention.)
d6 
Roll
Notable Item
1

Secret Loot (Storage Room, DC 15 Lockpick or 
Strength Check to Open)

High-Performance Racing Bike (75 SV) – 
Light and silent, but fragile.

Taser (1d4+stun, 30 SV) – Non-lethal but 
excellent for disabling enemies.

Raider Stash (Random) – If a survivor was 
hiding here, their stash contains 2d6 x 5 SV 
worth of various supplies.
Ambiguous Lore (What Really 
Happened Here?)
The apocalypse’s origins remain unclear, but Pedal 
Power contains eerie clues.
d4 Roll Lore Clue
1

an ID card reading “BioDyne 
Courier Division.”

A bike helmet covered in strange 
carvings, possibly occult in nature.
3
A half-written manifesto about 
“The Road Warriors” – a gang of 
cyclists obsessed with mobility in 
the apocalypse.
4
A mysterious receipt showing a 
high-tech order labeled “Project 
R.A.C.E.R.” with no further 
details.



zombies are drawn to the noise.



present, his gunfire immediately spikes 
Tension by 3d6.
Potential Enemies
(If enemies are present, use these stat blocks.)
Shamblers (2d4)

HP: 12 each

Attack: Bite (1d6, infection on failed Con save)


Crawler Zombies (1d4)

HP: 8

Special: Latches onto legs (Dex DC 13 to 
escape)


Cycling Dead (Brute on a Bike)




The Speed Freak (Deranged

HP: 18

AC: 13 (Leather)

Attack: Handgun (1d8 damage, 6 shots) OR 
Tire Iron (1d6 damage, can Disarm)

Special:
o
Speed Junkie: Always acts first in 
combat.
o
Obsessive Survivalist: If talked to 
(Charisma DC 16), may trade supplies 
instead of fighting.
o
If killed, his stash is found in the 
storage room.
Survival XP & Rewards

Securing the Shop: 200 SV

Negotiating with the Speed Freak instead of 
killing him: +150 SV

Using the bike shop to establish a “scout 
post” for mall movement: +250 SV over time

Leaving a bike for emergency escape 
purposes: +50 SV (for later use)
Special Optional 
Encounter: The “Road 
Warriors”
If the Tension Meter is 50+, an NPC faction called 
the Road Warriors may appear.
- They are a gang of nomadic cyclists who reject 
staying in one place.
- Leader: “Torque”, an ex-messenger who believes 
speed is survival.
- Trade Offer: If treated well, they offer bike 
modifications (+5ft speed per upgrade).
- Threat: If threatened, they will attempt to steal 
supplies and flee.
Final Notes
Pedal Power is a potentially valuable supply hub, but 
its open storefront and noise hazards make it 
dangerous.
- Smart players will reinforce the back room to use as 
a stash point.
- The Speed Freak can be a useful ally if handled 
well.
- Bicycles offer a fast escape option, but risk 
drawing attention in enclosed spaces.

sites.name: Root & Vine
sites.bookText:
Root & Vine (Shop #15)
“Nature  is  taking  back  what  was  once  hers.  This 
garden shop, once neat rows of potted plants and 
trellises, has become an overgrown jungle. Thick ivy 
coils around toppled shelves, while hanging ferns drip 
with condensation from a leaking skylight. The air is 
thick with the smell of damp earth and decay, mixed 
with  an  unexpected  sweetness—something  is 
blooming.  A  rustling  noise  from  the  back,  barely 
perceptible, suggests you are not alone. A shattered 
glass  window  in  the  rear  has  let  something…  or 
someone in.”
Description

Layout:
Root & Vine was once a boutique garden 
store specializing in exotic plants, small 
trees, and decorative garden décor. Now, it’s 
an overgrown tangle of plant life, with vines 
and roots creeping across the floor, cracked 
pots spilling their contents, and planters 
knocked over like barricades. A collapsed 
greenhouse display in the center of the shop 
has created a natural bottleneck, forcing 
anyone moving through to squeeze past 
sharp, broken glass.

Threats:
o
1d4 Shamblers (Hidden Among the 
Vines): These zombies are partially 
wrapped in foliage, making them hard 
to spot until disturbed.
o
1 Plant-Husk (Mutated Corpse, 
Rooted to the Floor): This former 
gardener has been overtaken by 
fungal growth, its body fused with the 
vines. If approached, it releases a 
cloud of hallucinogenic spores (CON 
save DC 13 or suffer disadvantage on 
Perception for 1 hour).

Hazards:
o
Thorned Ivy Patches: Moving 
through these areas without gloves or 
long sleeves deals 1d4 damage.
o
Rotten Floorboards: Some parts of 
the wooden floor are weakened by 
moisture. A character stepping on one 
must make a DC 12 Dexterity save or 
fall into a basement crawlspace 
(taking 1d6 damage and possibly 
disturbing a lurking corpse).
o
Leaking Skylight: Occasional drips of 
rainwater make the floor slippery—all 
Dex-based checks are at -2 penalty 
in affected areas.
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Gardener’s Machete (Melee, 1d8 
Slashing, Ignores Plant Cover) – 
Still sharp, though stained with dried 
blood.
2

Flammable, Improvised Weapon, 
2d6 Fire if ignited)
3
First Aid Kit (Moldy, Requires INT 
Check to Use Effectively, 10 SV)
4
Handmade Notebook (Weathered, 
contains strange botanical 
sketches** and survival notes) – 
Possible Ambiguous Lore.**
5

sustainable food source, +100 SV if 
secured in base)
6
Rusty Trowel (1d4 Piercing), 
Gardening Gloves (+2 vs. Thorn 
Damage), and Small Shears 
(Useful for traps, can cut wire or 
plant growth, 5 SV)
Ambiguous Lore
Scattered around the shop are clues hinting at 
multiple apocalyptic causes—all contradicting each 
other:
d4 
Roll

Survivalist Notes: A handwritten 
journal details someone’s attempt

to cultivate edible plants inside the 
mall. The last page reads: “The 
soil’s all wrong. Nothing grows right 
anymore. The roots are… moving.”
2

Damaged): A document stamped 
“CLASSIFIED” references an 
experiment called Project Bloom—
an attempt to engineer plants that 
could “purify the infected air.” It 
failed.
3

overturned planter. A note nearby 
reads: “The Green One’s roots run 
deep… life cannot be stopped, only 
reshaped.”

pathogen” before abruptly cutting 
off.

sites.name: Tech Haven
sites.bookText:
Tech Haven (Shop #16)
“The shattered remains of tablets and phones crunch 
underfoot as you step inside. Rows of display cases, 
once gleaming with the latest gadgets, are now dark 
and lifeless, their glass fronts cracked and smeared 
with  dried  blood.  A  bank  of  TV  screens  flickers 
erratically—some  showing  static,  others  displaying 
frozen emergency broadcasts. The air smells faintly 
of burnt circuits, and a tangled mess of wires drapes 
over  the  counter  like  a  nest  of  dead  serpents. 
Somewhere  deeper  in  the  store,  a  robotic  voice 
repeatedly  announces:  ‘Low  battery…  please 
recharge… Low battery… please recharge…’”
Description:

Layout: The store features a central 
checkout counter, multiple aisles lined with 
dead display models, a back storage room, 
and an employees-only repair workshop. A 
tangled mess of wires and broken glass make 
movement tricky.

Threats: 2d4 Shamblers lurk among the 
shelves, partially hidden by toppled displays. 
 233 

Lower Level
 
Zombie Mall
One of them wears a former employee’s blue 
polo, its nametag still clipped to its rotting 
chest.

Hazards:
o
Exposed Wires: Some areas have 
live wires sparking. Touching them 
causes 1d6 electrical damage and a 
20% chance of stunning (DEX Save 
DC 12 to avoid).
o
Collapsing Shelves: Heavy, unstable 
shelving could fall (STR Check DC 14 
to prevent).
o
Security Alarm (50% Chance): A 
tripwire near the checkout triggers the 
store’s failing security alarm, 
immediately raising Tension by 
+1d6 and attracting zombies from 
nearby stores.

“Emergency lockdown in progress. 
Please evacuate immediately.” and 
raises Tension by +2d4.
4
Trapped Survivor?! – A weak 
voice calls for help from the back 
storage room—but is it human or 
bait?
5
Power Surge – The store briefly 
regains power. Devices reboot, 
revealing more digital logs or a 
potentially dangerous

6
Strange Signal – The hand-crank 
radio picks up a broadcast from 
outside the mall: “We see you. 
Stay where you are. Help is 
coming.” But… is it?
Potential Escape Route:

Vents Behind the Repair Shop: Players can 
attempt to crawl through the ventilation 
system leading to another store.

Emergency Exit (Locked, STR DC 16 or 
Lockpicking DC 14 to Open): Leads to an 
employee-only corridor filled with unknown 
dangers.
Final Notes:
- Tech Haven is a goldmine for electronics, but 
dangerous due to unstable wiring, loud security 
systems, and malfunctioning AI.
- There’s a deep mystery tied to the tech store, 
especially if players investigate the USB drive, 
malfunctioning drones, and electronic logs.
- Smart survivors will use found technology for base 
defenses, traps, or surveillance.

sites.name: Beauty Bliss
sites.bookText:
Beauty Bliss (Shop #17)
“A sickly-sweet perfume lingers in the air, mingling 
with the scent of dust and something more rancid. 
Shelves  of  high-end  skincare  products  remain 
perfectly arranged, untouched by looters, their sleek 
packaging  gleaming  under  dim,  flickering  lights.  A 
shattered display case glitters with broken glass, its 
contents—luxury fragrances and makeup—scattered 
across the tile floor like a forgotten shrine to vanity. 
Headless mannequins, once adorned with the latest 
beauty  trends,  stand  eerily  in  the  corners,  their 
featureless  faces  reflecting  the  dim  glow  of 
emergency lighting. A distant clatter echoes from the 
backroom—something is still moving in here…”
General Description
Beauty Bliss was once an upscale cosmetics and 
skincare boutique, specializing in imported perfumes, 
luxury makeup, and overpriced facial treatments. Now, 
the store feels like an abandoned museum of excess, 
with its pristine products preserved behind glass while 
the rest of the world decays. The main floor is mostly 
intact, though overturned makeup counters and 
splintered display shelves hint at a struggle. The 
storage room in the back remains closed—something 
has been scratching at the door from the inside.

Hazard



not escalating Tension.

sites.name: Retro Revival
sites.bookText:
Retro Revival (Shop #18)
“The dim neon ‘Retro Revival’ sign still hums softly, 
casting an eerie greenish glow over the scattered 
shelves of vintage oddities. The store smells of old 
paper and dust, with rows of glass cases displaying 
antique trinkets, cracked vinyl records, and forgotten 
relics of a bygone era. A headless mannequin in a 
disco suit stands frozen mid-stride, its missing head 
replaced with a battered CRT television looping static. 
A  faded  ‘CLOSED’  sign  dangles  askew  on  the 
entrance  door—though  something  inside  suggests 
you’re not alone…”
General Description

Layout:
A cramped, cluttered space filled with narrow 
aisles of old furniture, display cases of 
collectibles, and walls lined with faded movie 
posters and classic arcade marquees. A 
storage room in the back remains ominously 
closed, its door slightly ajar.

Threats:
o
1d4 Shamblers lazily shuffle through 
the aisles, their movements 
occasionally setting off motion-
activated singing fish plaques mounted 
on the walls.
o
The Mannequin Horror – A twitching, 
animated mannequin wearing a 1970s 
leisure suit, indistinguishable from the 
others until it moves.

Hazards:
o
Creepy Music Box Trap: A survivor 
rigged an old music box to play upon 
entry. Stealth check DC 15 to disable, 
or it chimes loudly, adding +1d6 
Tension.
o
Wobbly Shelves: A poorly balanced 
display threatens to collapse if jostled 
(Strength DC 13 to stabilize, or a loud 
crash adds +2d6 Tension and knocks 
over anyone within 5 feet).
o
CRT Explosion: Some old televisions 
contain unstable cathode tubes. A 
heavy impact causes them to pop 
violently, dealing 1d4 piercing 
damage in a 5-ft radius.
Interactables & Loot
d6 Roll Notable Finds
1
Pristine Vinyl Record (50 SV) – A 
rare collector’s album worth trading.
2
Working Walkman + Cassette (25 
SV) – Can be used to distract 
zombies with music.
3
Vintage Baseball Bat (Improvised 
Weapon, 1d8 bludgeoning) – 
Well-worn but solid.
4
Survival Book: “Backyard 
Apocalypse” (75 SV, +1 Survival 
Check Bonus if studied).
5
Pocket Knife (1d4 slashing, 
Concealable, 10 SV).
6
Secret Stash in Back Room: A 
stash hidden in a jukebox (DC 15 
Investigation), containing $500 in 
useless cash, a revolver with 3 
bullets (35 SV), and a locked 
strongbox (DC 18 to open, 
contents unknown).
Ambiguous Lore (Roll 1d4 to 
Discover)
d4 
Roll
Cryptic Clue
1
A mummified hand clutches a 
scorched BioDyne Corporation ID 
badge, its nameplate scratched out.
2
A cassette tape labeled “DON’T 
LISTEN”. Playing it reveals garbled 
whispers and a distant heartbeat.
3
A vintage film reel contains a frame-
by-frame dissection of a zombie, 
 239 

Lower Level
 
Zombie Mall
labeled “Project Lazarus: Phase 
III”.
4
A mural behind a torn poster 
depicts a cosmic entity staring 
through a mall skylight, 
surrounded by people with hollow 
eyes. The word “AWAKEN” is 
scratched into the paint.
Tension Impact

Making Noise (breaking glass, setting off the 
music box, knocking over shelves) increases 
Tension by 1d6-2d6.

Searching for Loot takes 5 minutes per roll 
and carries a 25% chance per search to 
trigger a random event (see below).
Random Events (Roll 1d6 for 
Unexpected Situations)
d6 
Roll
Unexpected Event
1
The Mannequin Moves – That 
‘statue’ over there? Yeah, it just 
turned its head toward you.
2
Radio Signal – An old shortwave 
radio flickers to life with a garbled 
distress call: “If anyone… still out 
there… Roof… safe… but not for 
long…”
3
Mysterious Survivor Note – 
Scribbled on a receipt: “DON’T GO 
IN THE BACK ROOM. IT’S STILL IN 
THERE.”
4
The Power Flickers On – For 
exactly 30 seconds, the entire store 
lights up as if nothing had ever 
changed. Then… total darkness 
again.
5
Zombie Alarm – An old Furby in the 
toy section suddenly speaks. “Hee 
hee! Who’s there?” (Attracts 1d6 
zombies).
6
Door Slam – The storage room 
door slams shut by itself. 
Something inside is breathing.
Potential Enemies
Enemy 
Encounter
Description
1d4 Shamblers
Typical zombies, slow-
moving but dangerous in 
tight spaces.
The 
Mannequin 
Horror
Appears as an ordinary 
mannequin until 
approached. Attacks 
suddenly (Dex Save DC 14 
to avoid surprise round). 
Moves only when 
unobserved.
The Thing in 
the Back 
Room
A mass of fused limbs and 
faces (AC 14, HP 30, 2 
attacks per round, 
horrifying). Moves 
erratically and laughs when 
wounded.
Monster Stats (Key Threats)
The Mannequin Horror
(Ambush Predator, Undead Construct)
- AC: 12
- HP: 20
- MV: 0 when seen, 40 ft. when unobserved
- Attacks: Heavy Slam (1d8+2 bludgeoning)
- Special Abilities:
- Stillness: Remains indistinguishable from normal 
mannequins until attacked.
- Unseen Terror: Moves instantly whenever nobody 
is looking at it.
- Face of Fear: Any survivor who sees it move must 
make a DC 12 Wisdom save or freeze in fear for 1 
round.
The Thing in the Back Room (Aberrant Zombie 
Mass)

AC: 14
 240 

Zombie Mall
 
Lower Level

HP: 30

MV: 10 ft. (slow but inevitable)

Attacks:
o
Fused Limbs (2 attacks per round, 
1d6 bludgeoning + grapple)
o
Inhuman Laughter (Tension +3d6 
upon hearing it for the first time)
o
Regenerates 1d4 HP per round 
unless burned
XP & Survival Value (SV)
Action or Loot

Revival entirely

+50 SV
Vintage Collectibles 
(Vinyls, Old Tech)
50-100 SV per rare 
find
Final Notes
Retro Revival offers a mix of psychological horror, 
scavenging, and an unpredictable “haunted” 
atmosphere. Whether players stumble upon the 
Mannequin Horror, uncover some cryptic conspiracy 
clues, or simply grab a Walkman to blast zombie-
distracting tunes, this store provides both survival 
value and unsettling mysteries.
But the thing in the back room? Yeah, they probably 
shouldn’t open that door.

sites.name: Victory Sports
sites.bookText:
Victory Sports
“The entrance to this sporting goods store is wide 
open, its security gate jammed halfway down. Rows 
of sneakers, jerseys, and scattered duffel bags lie in 
disarray. Mannequins in athletic poses loom eerily in 
the  dim  light,  their  plastic  faces  frozen  in  mock 
determination. Blood smears stain the floor near the 
checkout counter, leading toward the dressing rooms. 
A faint scraping noise echoes from the aisles beyond, 
something—or someone—is still inside. The lingering 
scent of rubber and sweat mixes with something far 
less pleasant: the coppery tang of dried blood.”
Description

Layout: A wide, open store filled with athletic 
apparel, sporting equipment, and a shoe 
department in the back. There are narrow 
aisles cluttered with fallen racks, an employee 
breakroom, storage room, and dressing 
area where something has scratched at the 
inside of the doors.

Threats: (1d4+1) Shamblers wandering 
among mannequins, 1 Stalker Zombie hiding 
in a fitting room, waiting to lunge.

Hazards:
o
Loose Sporting Goods: Moving too 
fast may trip a survivor (Dexterity DC 
12 or fall prone).
o
Motion Sensor Lights: A 
malfunctioning security feature flickers 
on at random, increasing Tension by 
1d6 if zombies are nearby.
o
Barricaded Dressing Room: A 
survivor may be trapped inside—or 
something worse (Strength DC 14 to 
break open).

cracking skulls. (10 SV)

involving movement) – Speed is

on natural 20) – Surprisingly well-
kept. (40 SV)

(1d6 servings of food/water, each

rations. (Varies)
6
Sports Padding (Medium Armor,

– Repurposed football pads for

Ambiguous Lore
Among the scattered items, several clues hint at 
different possible causes of the apocalypse:
d4 Roll Lore Clue
1
Bloodstained Flyer: “Join 
BioDyne’s endurance trials—test 
your limits and push beyond!” with 
scrawled words underneath: “THEY

Sixth Seal is broken. The 
champions have fallen. The swarm 
comes next.”

unnatural speeds before the feed 
cuts out.
4

a withered husk of a former 
survivor, clutching a diary 
detailing a “new sickness” that 
turned his friend into an 
unstoppable runner.


Running & Loud Noises: Any sprinting inside 
the store increases Tension by 1d4 due to 
echoing footsteps.

Breaking into the Barricaded Dressing 
Room: Increases Tension by 2d6 if something 
is inside.

Firing Guns: Will immediately raise Tension 
by 3d6 due to echoes inside the mall.

Escape & Strategy

Players may secure the store as a training 
ground (grants temporary morale bonus)

If zombies are left alive, they will follow 
survivors to other locations.

Fast zombies and “Coach” can lead hordes 
elsewhere, forcing strategic retreats.
Summary

Victory Sports offers valuable melee 
weapons, armor, and stamina-based perks, 
but its open layout makes it dangerous.

Tension increases quickly if players aren’t 
careful.

Dressing rooms provide an optional horror 
encounter.

Enemies vary from basic shamblers to 
terrifying sprinting undead.
Clearing and fortifying this store could turn it into a 
useful outpost… but only if survivors can handle 
the horrors lurking inside.

sites.name: Bargain Bin
sites.bookText:
Bargain Bin (Shop #20)
“The Bargain Bin is a chaotic mess of overstuffed 
shelves, teetering piles of clothing, and scattered bins 
filled  with  unsorted  junk.  Fluorescent  lights  flicker 
overhead, casting eerie shadows across aisles filled 
with  forgotten  trinkets  and  abandoned  holiday 
decorations.  A  faded  banner  still  hangs  from  the 
ceiling—‘EVERYTHING MUST GO!’—now more of a 
grim prophecy than a sales pitch. The musty smell of 
old fabric, mildew, and something faintly rotten fills 
the air. Somewhere deeper in the store, a rhythmic 
tapping sound echoes, like someone—or something
—sifting through the debris…”
Description

Layout: A sprawling, cluttered thrift store with 
narrow, winding aisles. The floor is covered in 
discarded clothing, broken toys, and 
miscellaneous junk. A checkout counter with an 
ancient register sits near the front, and a dimly 
lit backroom serves as a storage area.

Threats: (Roll 1d6)
1-2: 1d4 Shamblers are tangled in clothing 
racks, sluggish but numerous.
3-4: A Stalker Zombie lurks near the back, 
hiding behind mannequins, waiting to pounce.
5: A Deranged Hoarder (hostile survivor) is 
guarding their stash, armed with a box cutter.
6: A Rotting Mannequin—a zombie that 
stands eerily still until players approach.

Hazards:
o
Trip Hazards: Loose wires, collapsed 
shelves, and unstable furniture make 
movement difficult. (Dexterity DC 13 to 
avoid falling prone if running.)
o
Mannequin Confusion: Some 
mannequins are just mannequins… 
but are they all? (Roll 1d6 per 
mannequin. On a 6, it’s actually a 
disguised zombie.)
o
Noise Traps: Rummaging through the 
junk risks knocking over precarious 
stacks. Roll 1d4: On a 1, an avalanche 
of objects crashes loudly, increasing 
Tension by 1d6.

sites.name: Fantasy Wardrobe
sites.bookText:
Fantasy Wardrobe (Shop 
#21)
“A rainbow of forgotten dreams hangs on metal racks
—superhero  capes,  wizard  robes,  and  knightly 
tabards draped in dust and mold. Plastic mannequins 
stand frozen mid-pose, adorned in battle-worn power 
armor or flowing anime cloaks, their lifeless gazes 
eerily fixed on the entrance. The scent of stale fabric 
and cheap polyester lingers in the air. Somewhere in 
the back, a faint scraping noise echoes—a sound too 
steady, too rhythmic, to be the wind.”
General Description
Fantasy Wardrobe was once a haven for cosplayers 
and fandom enthusiasts, filled with elaborate costumes, 
accessories, and replica weapons. Now, it has become 
a surreal battlefield of cloth and plastic, where tattered 
outfits and cracked masks create unsettling silhouettes 
in the flickering emergency lights. Torn dressing rooms 
offer glimpses of movement in cracked mirrors. The 
checkout counter is barricaded with mannequin limbs 
and costume racks, suggesting someone tried to hold 
out here… and failed.
Encounter Elements
Environmental Hazards & Traps (roll 1d4 on entry)
d4 Roll
Hazard
1
Falling Costume Racks: A 
precarious shelf collapses when 
bumped (DEX DC 13 or take 1d6 
bludgeoning, +1d4 Tension).
2
Glowing Eyes in the Dark: A 
malfunctioning animatronic knight 
starts moving its head toward the 
survivors. It does nothing… but for 
how long? (Raises Tension by 
+1d6.)
3
Mirror Illusions: The cracked 
mirrors distort reflections 
unnaturally—sometimes showing 
figures that aren’t there. WIS DC 
14 to resist paranoia.
4
Mannequin Maze: Moving 
 246 

Zombie Mall
 
Lower Level
through the back room requires 
a DEX DC 12 check to navigate. 
A failure means knocking over 
mannequins and making noise 
(+1d6 Tension).

d6 Roll Notable Items
1
Foam Replica Sword – 
Lightweight but intimidating; can be 
used as a bluff or distraction. (No 
damage, but good for RP)
2
Plastic Power Armor – Useless for 
protection but offers +1 
Intimidation when worn.
3
Real Chainmail (Hidden in 
Storage) – Counts as Medium 
Armor (AC 14, disadvantage on 
Stealth).
4
Prop Firearm (Looks Real) – Can 
be used for deception (CHA DC 15 
to fool enemies into thinking it’s 
loaded).
5
Utility Belt (From a Superhero 
Costume) – Contains rope, fake 
grappling hook, and a pouch of 
coins (Worth 25 SV).
6
Blood-Stained Note – A frantic 
message scrawled on the back of 
a receipt: “They’re still in the 
dressing rooms. Don’t open the 
doors.” (Ambiguous Lore)
Ambiguous Lore:
Scattered clues hint at multiple conflicting explanations 
for the apocalypse. Survivors exploring the shop might 
find:
d4 Roll Lore Clue
1
Costume Design Notes: A receipt 
for a rush order of “Reaper Cultist 
Robes,” with a customer name that 
matches a missing persons report.
2
Military Warning Flyer: A wrinkled 
evacuation notice marked 
“Containment Protocol Theta” 
suggests the government knew 
about this in advance.
3
A Smiling Mannequin Holding a 
Cultist Dagger: An ornate blade 
sits in its stiff grip. Who placed it 
there… and why?
4
Mall Security Memo: A security 
log references complaints about 
“strange figures after closing 
hours” who left cryptic symbols 
on dressing room mirrors.
Tension Impact
Actions taken inside Fantasy Wardrobe can increase 
the Mall’s Tension Meter, drawing more zombies.

Knocking over costume racks (+1d4 
Tension)

Moving past mirrors and seeing 
“something” that isn’t there (+1d6 Tension)

Attempting to open the locked dressing 
rooms (+2d6 Tension)

Finding and activating the store’s old 
speaker system (plays unsettling carnival 
music) (+3d6 Tension, automatically alerts 
nearby zombies)
Potential Enemies
d6 
Roll
Encounter
1-2
1d4 Shamblers in Costume: These 
zombies wear tattered cosplay 
outfits, making them oddly theatrical 
in their movements.
3
Dressing Room Horror: A long-
trapped zombie, perfectly still, 
waiting inside a dressing room. If 
opened, it lunges with advantage 
on its first attack.
 247 

Lower Level
 
Zombie Mall
4
Mannequin Stalker: Not a zombie, 
but something is wrong with it. It 
never moves when watched… but 
every time you turn around, it is 
closer.
5
“The Knight” (Zombie Brute in 
Armor): A former security guard in 
full convention-grade plate mail, 
now undead. Has DR 3 vs melee 
and hits hard.
6
Possessed Mannequin (Special 
Horror Creature): Moves silently 
and unpredictably. Can only be 
harmed if survivors first smash 
its mask, revealing an empty, 
screaming void beneath.

Final Notes & Story Hooks

Rival Survivor Faction Interest: A survivor 
group might be looking for convention-grade 
armor or weapons, thinking they will help in 
battle.

NPC Survivor Connection: A missing 
person’s flyer outside the mall features 
someone wearing a very specific cosplay

of them.


who put it on hear whispers encouraging them 
to stay… forever.
